title: Ruth 3:18.
paragraphs:
Ruth 3:18.
“Then Naomi said, ‘Wait, my daughter, until you learn how the matter turns out, for the man will not rest but will settle the matter today.’”
This verse is quiet.
But it is loaded.
Ruth had done all she could. She obeyed. She stepped out in faith. She placed the matter in Boaz’s hands. Now Naomi gives her one hard command:
Wait.
That hurts, doesn’t it?

Because faith is not only walking onto the threshing floor.
Faith is also sitting still when your future is unresolved.

Naomi knew Boaz’s character.
He was not casual.
Not passive.
Not playing games.
“He will not rest.”
And that line whispers something bigger than Boaz.
It points us to Christ.

Jesus is the greater Boaz who does not leave redemption unfinished. He does not start a saving work and then abandon the soul that came under His covering. He moves with purpose. He settles what sin complicated. He finishes what grace began.

So Ruth 3:18 is not just about patience.
It is about trusting the Redeemer while heaven seems silent.

You may be in that kind of verse right now.
No answer yet.
No closure yet.
No visible breakthrough yet.
But here’s what we miss:

Waiting is not abandonment.
Waiting is often the room where God proves His faithfulness.

Ruth did not need to chase Boaz.
She needed to trust his resolve.

And child of God, you do not need to panic your way into peace.
You need to trust the finished heart of Christ.

Hope point:
What concerns you deeply does not escape the Redeemer’s attention. Jesus is not restless with anxiety, but He is fully committed to completing your redemption and keeping His promises.
“Wait, my daughter.”

That is not a dismissal.
That is comfort.
Because when the right Redeemer is handling the matter, hope can breathe.

Prayer:
Lord Jesus, when my heart wants to run ahead, teach me to wait in faith. Remind me that You do not leave redemption unfinished. Settle what I cannot settle, and anchor me in Your faithfulness. Amen.
